Diagnose selection reliability of a fitted STABL object

Source: R/diagnostics.R
stabl_diagnose.Rd

Inspects a stabl_fit result and returns a structured stabl_diagnostics object: score-distribution summaries, decoy-generator provenance, the full threshold path of real/decoy selection counts, FDP+ curve features (selected cut-off, ties, flat minima, boundary solutions, low-decoy-count instability), a null-saturation probe, a score-dependence assumption probe, and a learner x decoy x outcome x dimensionality evidence profile with benchmark provenance.

Usage

stabl_diagnose(
  fit,
  ...,
  saturation_threshold = 0.05,
  saturation_proportion = 0.5,
  low_decoy_count = 5L
)

Arguments

fit

A fitted stabl_fit() object (including stabl() results, which inherit from stabl_fit).

...

Reserved for future use; passing arguments here is an error.

saturation_threshold

Numeric in [0, 1]; thresholds at or below this value are considered "near-zero" for the null-saturation probe. Default 0.05.

saturation_proportion

Numeric in (0, 1]; the probe flags null-like saturation when a near-zero threshold selects at least this proportion of real and of artificial features. Default 0.5.

low_decoy_count

Non-negative integer; the FDP+ minimum is flagged as unstable when the artificial-feature count at the selected threshold is below this value. Default 5L.

Value

An object of class stabl_diagnostics with components:

score_summary

List of distribution summaries (quantiles, mean) for real and artificial per-feature maximum scores.

decoy_provenance

The fit's artificial_provenance (requested vs actual generator, fallback counts), or NULL.

threshold_path

data.frame with threshold, n_real, n_artificial, prop_real, prop_artificial, and fdp_plus along the full fdr_threshold_range.

per_lambda

data.frame of per-lambda real/artificial selected counts at the selected threshold (regularization-path view).

cutoff

List describing the selected threshold, the selection rule in effect ("user_hard_threshold", "fdp_plus_minimum", or "none"), the comparator, and the FDP+ denominator convention.

fdp_curve

List with the FDP+ curve, all minimizing thresholds, and tie/flat/boundary flags.

null_saturation

List with the null-saturation probe result.

dependence_probe

List with score-profile correlation summaries (assumption probe only).

evidence_profile

data.frame of matching evidence rows with status and provenance.

warning_codes

Character vector of machine-readable codes.

assumption_notes

Character vector of assumption statements.

calibration_scope

Character vector delimiting what the FDP+ diagnostic does and does not establish.

Details

The diagnostic is read-only: it never changes the fit or its selected support. It distinguishes a user-supplied hard_threshold from the minimized-FDP+ rule and reports the effective threshold comparator (strict >) and the FDP+ denominator convention (n_artificial / artificial_proportion + 1) / pmax(1, n_real).

See also

compute_fdp_plus(), plot_fdr_graph(), get_support()

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 8), 60, 8,
            dimnames = list(paste0("s", 1:60), paste0("f", 1:8)))
y <- setNames(x[, 1] * 2 + rnorm(60), rownames(x))
fit <- stabl_fit(x, y, n_bootstraps = 20, lambda_grid = "auto",
                 artificial_type = "random_permutation")
d <- stabl_diagnose(fit)
d$warning_codes
#> [1] "STABL_DIAG_TIED_MINIMA"           "STABL_DIAG_FLAT_MINIMUM"         
#> [3] "STABL_DIAG_BOUNDARY_MINIMUM"      "STABL_DIAG_HIGH_SCORE_DEPENDENCE"
#> [5] "STABL_DIAG_EMPTY_SUPPORT"
